blocks.prompt: 4 How many signals can be given by 6 flags of different colours, using 2 flags at a time?
blocks.explanation:
A signal is made by hoisting 2 flags one above the other; the order (top, bottom) changes the signal.
We must count the signals.
Plan: choose and arrange 2 of the 6 flags: \({}^{6}P_{2}\).
steps:
Given: 6 flags of different colours, 2 used at a time.
To find: the number of signals.
Method: Red above blue is a different signal from blue above red, so order matters: use \({}^{n}P_{r}\) with \(n = 6\), \(r = 2\).

Use the formula
\[{}^{6}P_{2} = \dfrac{6!}{(6-2)!} = \dfrac{6!}{4!}\]
\[= \dfrac{6 \cdot 5 \cdot 4!}{4!} = 6 \cdot 5\]
Why: \(6! = 6 \cdot 5 \cdot 4!\), so \(4!\) cancels.

Check
Box method: top position 6 choices, bottom position 5 choices (one flag is already used): \(6 \times 5 = 30\) \(\checkmark\)
Why: The same flag cannot be used twice.
